data.title: Etsy updates AI policy, noting concerns about buyer trust
data.description:
Etsy published updated guidelines on artificial intelligence (AI) for sellers on Oct. 22. The marketplace is restricting specific categories of AI-generated content, tightening listing photo requirements and introducing new enforcement tools.

The changes signal a larger effort to protect buyer trust, which Etsy says is being eroded as AI-generated listings proliferate across the platform.

“AI should support your creativity and craftsmanship, not replace them,” Etsy vice president of customer operations James Ossman wrote in the update. “Buyers should always be able to understand the role you play in every item you sell on Etsy.”

Etsy is No. 20 in Digital Commerce360’s Global Online Marketplaces Database. The market research tool ranks the 100 largest marketplaces by third-party gross merchandise value (GMV).

How Etsy’s new AI guidelines work

Etsy’s seller handbook now includes a categorical ban on AI-generated functional guides, including patterns, recipes or instructions. Listings for these items must also show a real result made using the seller’s own instructions, not an AI-generated image of what the finished product might look like.

In addition, Etsy now requires that every listing include at least one unedited photo of the actual item against a real background. Supplemental images can still use AI-assisted editing to adjust lighting, color, cropping or backgrounds, but all photos must accurately represent the item a buyer will receive.

Notably, the marketplace is not banning AI-generated art outright. The policy continues to allow it when sellers play a clear creative role in its creation, such as a fantasy illustration based on the seller’s own prompt and creative direction. Sellers must still disclose when an item is created using AI and cannot misrepresent AI-generated work as handmade.

Bot-generated listings without human involvement are explicitly prohibited and will result in listing removal, Etsy said.

How Etsy will enforce the new rules

Meanwhile, Etsy says it will alert sellers if it detects AI-generated images during the listing process. It intends to provide guidance to help sellers meet requirements.

Looking ahead, the marketplace said it will expand that detection to existing listings over time. Sellers whose listings are removed can appeal through the Policy violations page in Etsy’s Shop Manager options.

Etsy is also adding a new buyer-facing reporting option so consumers can flag listings that they believe are AI-generated. Those reports will initially inform Etsy’s understanding of how buyers perceive AI misuse, rather than trigger immediate enforcement action, with removal activity expanding in the coming months as detection tools improve.

Etsy’s evolving relationship with AI

As it tightens AI restrictions on sellers, Etsy also continues to use AI itself. 

As Digital Commerce 360 reported in August, CEO Kruti Goyal described Etsy’s AI strategy as focused on three areas: improving product discovery, delivering more personalized shopping experiences, and experimenting with agentic and conversational commerce. 

“We see the biggest opportunity for AI on Etsy itself,” Goyal said on the company’s Q2 earnings call. “It’s really about using AI to make Etsy much, much better at connecting the right buyers with the right sellers.”

Etsy has partnered with OpenAI, Google and Microsoft on agentic commerce,  announced it would sell directly through Google AI Mode in January and is a backer of Google’s Agent Payments Protocol. Goyal said in August that agentic AI experiences still account for less than 1% of Etsy’s traffic, though the referrals that do come through AI channels carry higher buyer intent and average order value than typical traffic.

In 2025, Etsy rolled out AI-powered tools for sellers, including a writing assistant that mimics a seller’s voice, bulk listing suggestions and AI-generated review highlights.

data.title: Staples Canada launches Staples Business to unify B2B offerings
data.description:
Staples Canada has launched Staples Business, a new brand in the market to bring office supplies, technology, print and facilities services together for Canadian business customers.

The brand will focus on two tiers: one for smaller businesses and one for larger buyers that need custom pricing and dedicated account support.

Richmond Hill, Ontario-based Staples Canada said the new brand would simplify purchasing and account management for business customers.

Why Staples Business is launching in Canada

“Staples Business brings everything our business customers rely on together under one brand, building on our long-standing commitment to supporting Canadian businesses for more than 30 years,” said Chris Saniga, chief B2B officer at Staples Canada. “As a Canadian company, we understand the pressures organizations here are facing. Whether it’s a growing startup or a large enterprise, our goal is to take more off their plate so they can focus on what comes next.”

Currently, Staples has nearly 300 outlets in Canada. Its Quebec stores operate under the Bureau en Gros nameplate.

Industry analysts assessed that the new brand’s debut is as much about competition as customer service.

Marty Bauer, ecommerce expert at Omnisend, an email and SMS marketing platform for ecommerce brands, said the move was necessary to fend off competition.

“This new branding strategy is about much more than a cosmetic rebrand,” Bauer stated. “It’s an important step in defending the market against ecommerce giants, particularly Amazon Business.”

What makes Staples Canada’s business customer unique?

Bauer noted that B2B clients are quite different from regular shoppers in Staples Canada’s case.

“The goal is to make supply procurement as easy and frictionless as possible,” he said. “It’s as much about time and efficiency as it is about price. The new, refreshed Staples Business aims to offer exactly that.”

Bauer added that Staples Business has brought together a wide range of products, from office and janitorial supplies to IT hardware.

“This means a single account manager is responsible for all of a client’s needs, which significantly lowers administrative hassle for both parties,” Bauer said.

Additionally, Bauer pointed out that Staples Business will be able to categorize its clients into different tiers. Different-sized businesses require different approaches. For instance, small-to-medium businesses (SMBs) may place greater emphasis on an automated checkout system, transparency and fast response times than larger companies. Meanwhile, large businesses, Bauer explained, expect dynamic contract pricing, custom product catalogs and dedicated account managers.

“Staples Business is now better able to cater to these different needs,” Bauer said.

How Staples Business will try to compete in Canada

Lastly, Bauer said, a dedicated B2B brand could show Staples Canada’s business customers that a company is serious about catering to them and can compete with ecommerce giants.

“They may not be able to compete in terms of pricing, but they can compete in terms of expertise and the ability to cater to clients’ specific needs,” Bauer said.

Another observer said the brand’s success will depend on whether Staples can deliver on its promise.

Rich Pleeth, founder of the artificial intelligence (AI)-powered logistics platform Finmile, said a dedicated business brand can help Staples Canada win customers by making its wider offer easier to understand.

“Someone who thinks of Staples for printer paper may not think of it for IT support or facilities supplies,” Pleeth stated. “Putting those services together gives the sales team a clearer story, but the customer still needs a reason to change suppliers.”

Pleeth echoed Bauer’s perspective, adding that a small business might be persuaded by the prospect of less time spent ordering and chasing deliveries.

“For a larger buyer, consolidated invoicing, agreed pricing and an account manager who can sort out a problem could be worth more than a small discount on stationery,” Pleeth said. “The two tiers make sense because those buyers need different levels of support.”

Nevertheless, Pleeth expects that the new name will present a test.

“If a business orders laptops, chairs and printed materials for a new office, can someone coordinate the delivery and resolve anything missing?” he asked. “If the customer still has to chase three departments, the brand has promised more than the operation delivers.”

data.title: Parts Town Unlimited names new CIO and chief accounting officer to leadership team
data.description:
Equipment distributor Parts Town Unlimited named two new executives to its leadership team, including a chief information officer (CIO) to oversee its digital efforts.

The CIO role will belong to Pat Quint. Meanwhile, Kristi Belhumeur is taking on new duties as the company’s chief accounting officer.

The moves come more than a year after Parts Town CEO Bill Geary was named to the distributor’s top position. Geary noted the importance of both hires in a released statement.

Who is Parts Town Unlimited’s new CIO?

“Pat’s proven ability to turn technology into a strategic growth engine and unlock the full potential of AI-driven innovation, combined with Kristi’s deep expertise in multi-billion-dollar M&A transactions and finance transformation, makes them exceptional additions to our global leadership team,” said Geary. “Their leadership strengthens our ability to scale globally, accelerate growth and deepen the expertise needed to capitalize on new opportunities and drive long-term success.”

Most recently, Quint served in the CIO role at the global industrial manufacturing solutions provider Duravant. That followed a previous term as CIO at Mastronardi Produce.

Going forward, Parts Town Unlimited will look to Quint to execute its technology strategy. That strategy includes crucial automation and AI-powered technology, such as Parts Town’s PartPredictor tool, which received new features in 2026.

“It’s a privilege to work at Parts Town Unlimited given the impressive history, talented team, innovative solutions and focus on exceeding customer expectations,” Quint stated in Parts Town Unlimited’s announcement. “I look forward to helping the company achieve their goals by leveraging technology.”

Parts Town Unlimited’s chief accounting officer

Belhumeur, a certified public accountant, will bring 25 years of leadership experience in her field to Parts Town Unlimited. There, she will lead work for its global accounting, tax and treasury organizations, the company shared.

“Parts Town Unlimited has built an extraordinary business, and I look forward to applying my global finance leadership experience to help accelerate growth, support strategic expansion and deliver outstanding results for team members, customers and partners,” said Belhumeur.

Parts Town Unlimited noted that in addition to supporting mergers and acquisitions, Belhumeur will bolster audit and enterprise readiness at the company. She comes to Parts Town Unlimited after nearly two years as chief accounting officer at the janitorial supplies, foodservice, and industrial packaging distributor BradyPlus.

Parts Town Unlimited also serves the foodservice sector, in addition to its distribution of residential appliances and heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) equipment.

data.title: DoorDash to acquire Instacart in $17 billion grocery delivery deal
data.description:
DoorDash Inc. announced a deal to acquire its last-mile delivery rival Instacart in a deal valued at $17 billion.

The combined company would unite operations from two of the most active platforms in retail and grocery delivery services through a transaction subject to approval by regulators and Instacart shareholders. DoorDash expects to use a combination of cash, stock and debt to finance the deal. As a result, the acquisition would enable DoorDash to leverage Instacart’s technology and expertise.

Why DoorDash is acquiring Instacart

“Grocery is one of the hardest things to get right online,” said Tony Xu, co-founder and CEO of DoorDash, in the acquisition announcement. “Someone has to pick a ripe avocado, find a substitute you’d choose yourself, and get the ice cream to you before it melts.”

Xu praised the work that Instacart has done to date.

“Instacart has spent years learning to do that well for grocers, while DoorDash has built a delivery network and technology that local stores rely on every day,” he stated. “Together, we could give stores of every size more of those tools and unlock the potential of grocery delivery. It’s still early innings, but we know that when more people shop local, more dollars stay local.”

Online grocery sales in the U.S. grew by more than 20% year over year, increasing their share of total grocery spending, according to data tracked by the firm Brick Meets Click.

What comes next for Instacart

DoorDash and Instacart expect the deal to close near the end of 2027 or in the first half of 2028, the companies disclosed. After that, DoorDash expects to preserve the Instacart brand, along with its enterprise technology products and app. In the meantime, Instacart intends to continue to operate independently.

“Over the last 14 years, Instacart has transformed online grocery by helping retailers of all sizes compete and grow, and joining forces with DoorDash allows us to do even more,” said Chris Rogers, CEO of Instacart. “When our purpose-built grocery technology and trusted retailer and brand relationships are combined with DoorDash’s global consumer reach and logistics capabilities, we can create new opportunities for our retail and brand partners, offer an even better experience for customers and shoppers, and deliver compelling value for our shareholders.”

In the announcement, DoorDash noted that it could make 50,000 additional stores available to Instacart users through the deal, adding to almost 100,000 stores that already participate on Instacart’s platform.

data.title: Bose acquires Skullcandy in push to broaden audio brand portfolio
data.description:
Bose Corporation reached a deal to acquire fellow headphones brand Skullcandy, the companies formally announced on Oct. 21. The acquisition brings together two big names in consumer electronics and audio wearables, following a history of collaboration.

Bose is No. 103 in Digital Commerce 360’s Top 1000 Database. The market research tool tracks North America’s largest online retailers by their annual ecommerce sales. There, Skullcandy is No. 627.
